examples.scenario: A 25 cm DTM cell size is reported as ±25 cm vertical accuracy.
examples.reason: Raster cell size and vertical accuracy are different quantities; EA reports the same ±15 cm RMSE across multiple DTM resolutions.

examples.scenario: A 2 m composite is assumed less vertically accurate than a 1 m composite solely because the cells are larger.
examples.reason: The published survey RMSE is not derived from raster cell size alone.

examples.scenario: EA ±15 cm RMSE is presented as a guaranteed maximum error for every pixel.
examples.reason: RMSE is an error statistic/specification, not a per-pixel hard maximum bound.

examples.scenario: EA ±5 cm relative/random error is presented as absolute vertical accuracy.
examples.reason: EA explicitly distinguishes absolute RMSE from relative/random error.

examples.scenario: Ground-truth point ±3 cm RMSE is copied as the LiDAR dataset accuracy.
examples.reason: Reference-point uncertainty and LiDAR comparison error are distinct.

examples.scenario: OSGM15 8 mm RMS is reported as the total DTM elevation accuracy.
examples.reason: The geoid model is only one component of the vertical chain.

examples.scenario: EA ±15 cm RMSE and OSGM15 8 mm RMS are simply added arithmetically with no uncertainty model.
examples.reason: Different components require consistent standard-uncertainty interpretation and correlation policy.

examples.scenario: EA ±15 cm and OSGM15 8 mm are root-sum-squared while assuming independence without evidence.
examples.reason: NIST requires covariance/correlation treatment when components are correlated.

examples.scenario: A common vertical datum bias at both parcel extrema is assumed to cancel perfectly.
examples.reason: Common-mode cancellation depends on correlation and sensitivity and must be justified.

examples.scenario: The same common vertical-datum component is independently added to both max and min and double-counted.
examples.reason: Shared components must be represented once through the covariance-aware measurand model.

examples.scenario: Max and min local random errors are assumed independent because they are different cells.
examples.reason: Spatially related raster errors may be correlated; independence must be supported rather than presumed.

examples.scenario: A published specification is labelled as Type A uncertainty for the target parcel.
examples.reason: Type A requires statistical evaluation of observations; external specifications are Type B-style inputs unless target observations exist.

examples.scenario: A target-specific repeated-survey standard deviation is mixed with a manufacturer/specification uncertainty without class labels.
examples.reason: Different uncertainty sources must remain auditable even when both are converted to standard uncertainties.

examples.scenario: An uncertainty quoted in centimetres is combined numerically with a metre-valued component without unit normalization.
examples.reason: All components must share consistent units before propagation.

examples.scenario: A ±15 cm RMSE source specification is converted to 95% using 1.96 automatically.
examples.reason: The multiplier depends on the reporting standard and statistical assumptions; USGS terminology changed in 2024.

examples.scenario: A legacy USGS ACCz relation is applied to EA data without naming the standard/version.
examples.reason: Accuracy definitions must be version- and authority-specific.

examples.scenario: k=2 is used and the dashboard says exactly 95% confidence with no distribution assumptions.
examples.reason: NIST describes k≈2 as approximately 95% under suitable assumptions.

examples.scenario: Expanded uncertainty is shown without the coverage factor k.
examples.reason: Reporting must include k or state combined standard uncertainty instead.

examples.scenario: A source-chain readiness score of 99.99% is displayed as measurement accuracy.
examples.reason: Readiness is an internal preparation metric, not geospatial positional accuracy.

examples.scenario: A source confidence score of 99.99% is displayed as probability that the parcel height is correct.
examples.reason: Source confidence and measurement coverage probability are unrelated metrics.

examples.scenario: The 10 m composite inherits the ±15 cm survey RMSE and is therefore treated as equivalent to native 1 m DTM for extrema.
examples.reason: Resampling and coarse-cell representation remain separate processing effects.

examples.scenario: Bilinear resampling is ignored because input surveys met ±15 cm RMSE.
examples.reason: Input survey accuracy does not erase transformation/resampling effects.

examples.scenario: Different acquisition epochs are composited and represented by a single uncertainty component with no lineage record.
examples.reason: Survey lineage can change local error behavior and must remain traceable.

examples.scenario: Point density is used as a direct centimetre accuracy estimate.
examples.reason: EA treats point density, raster resolution and vertical accuracy as separate properties.

examples.scenario: A 25 cm raster is assumed more accurate than a 50 cm raster even when both come from the same survey QA class.
examples.reason: Finer sampling does not automatically reduce vertical measurement error.

examples.scenario: RMSE is described as standard deviation of all possible parcel errors with no bias discussion.
examples.reason: RMSE can include bias and spread; its use in an uncertainty budget must match the defined model.

examples.scenario: The uncertainty budget is computed before the actual max and min pixels are known.
examples.reason: The max-minus-min measurand and component correlations depend on the executed extrema result.

examples.scenario: A parcel-specific uncertainty interval is generated while canonical point rows are zero.
examples.reason: Static source specifications do not create a parcel-specific result.

examples.scenario: The same numeric height difference appears on two replays but component/covariance ledgers differ.
examples.reason: Equal numeric output does not prove equivalent uncertainty provenance.

examples.scenario: Primary and independent uncertainty-policy digests differ but the smaller interval is chosen.
examples.reason: Policy disagreement must fail closed rather than select the more favorable interval.

examples.scenario: ISO 19157 is cited as defining a minimum acceptable vertical accuracy for the project.
examples.reason: ISO 19157 describes data-quality evaluation/reporting but does not define universal minimum quality levels.

examples.scenario: The known runner ACK blocker is relabelled pending to make the dashboard appear active.
examples.reason: A known unresolved blocker remains BLOCKED; pending stays zero.

examples.scenario: A second runner is launched to calculate uncertainty while the canonical runner ACK is absent.
examples.reason: The continuation contract permits only the existing single shared runner.

examples.scenario: Static uncertainty preparation is reported as a measured vertical-accuracy result.
examples.reason: No parcel-specific measurement exists until canonical runtime sampling occurs.

examples.scenario: A height-difference confidence interval is produced from source RMSE alone while pixel membership and extrema tie sets are unresolved.
examples.reason: Membership and extrema selection are part of the executed measurand definition.

examples.scenario: Batch 75 is described as increasing target elevation accuracy from 99.99% to 100%.
examples.reason: The batch improves validation/readiness coverage; measured target elevation accuracy remains uncomputed.
